answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to stake a unique physical-token bond: a small marble of certified ivory sourced only from a monitored river-bed deposit. The protocol verifies the marble’s isotopic signature against a public ledger of river yields; an attacker must therefore acquire and chemically fingerprint fresh ivory for every fake identity, raising the marginal cost linearly with the number of sybils and making large-scale identity farming economically irrational.
